# logseq

A Logseq markdown graph: pages, journals and blocks, read and written as files.

- **Runs in:** the harness process
- **Source:** [lisp/modules/harness-logseq.el](../../lisp/modules/harness-logseq.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** nothing
- **Required by:** [workspace-knowledge](workspace-knowledge.md)

## About

A small, strict client for a Logseq graph kept as markdown files.  A
graph is a directory with `pages/` and `journals/` in it (the layout
`LOGSEQ_HOME` names); a page is one markdown file, a block is one
bullet, and properties are `key:: value` lines under it.  The module
knows nothing about workspaces, tools or memory policy: it reads and
writes pages, searches blocks and answers backlinks.

The format is the one Logseq renders, and the rules of the
repository's Logseq skill: every content line belongs to a `- `
bullet, children are indented under their parent, properties sit
under the bullet they describe, and page references are `[[Page]]`
links.  No markdown headers and no `---` separators are ever written:
Logseq does not render them as part of its outline.

A page's name is its path under `pages/` without the extension, so
`Threads/Kitchen renovation` is `pages/Threads/Kitchen renovation.md`:
`/` is Logseq's namespace separator and becomes a directory.  A name
Logseq would rewrite (a `#`, `[`, `|`, a control character) is
normalized before it becomes a file, and the name the caller writes
is the name reported back.

Writes are read, changed and renamed into place
(`harness-write-file-atomically`), one at a time in this process.
The user's own Logseq editor is the only other writer, and Logseq's
own lock is the boundary; this module never parses or touches
`logseq/` inside a graph, and never deletes a page or a block.

There is no index here.  A search reads the graph's pages and
returns the blocks that match, the best first.  The graph is the
source of truth; a later stage may add a cache in front of it
without changing this contract.

## Provides

### Methods

- `logseq/backlinks` (name &optional opts) — Return the blocks of the graph at OPTS' `:root` that link page NAME.
- `logseq/block-add` (page text &optional opts) — Append TEXT as a block of PAGE in the graph at OPTS' `:root`.
- `logseq/page` (name &optional opts) — Return page NAME of the graph at OPTS' `:root`, or nil.
- `logseq/page-add` (page text &optional opts) — Add TEXT as a block of PAGE, creating the page with OPTS' properties.
- `logseq/page-list` (&optional opts) — Return the pages of the graph at OPTS' `:root`, newest first.
- `logseq/property-set` (page key value &optional opts) — Set property KEY of PAGE to VALUE, in the page's identity block.
- `logseq/root` (&optional graph) — Return the graph GRAPH as a directory, or the configured one.
- `logseq/search` (query &optional opts) — Return the blocks of the graph at OPTS' `:root` that match QUERY.
- `logseq/status` (&optional root) — Return what the graph at ROOT says about itself.

### Options

- `harness-logseq-directory` — Root of the Logseq graph, or nil to find it.
- `harness-logseq-journal-format` — Format of a journal page's name, as `format-time-string` reads it.
- `harness-logseq-journal-pages` — Most journal files one search reads, the newest.
- `harness-logseq-journals-directory` — Directory of a graph's journal pages, relative to its root.
- `harness-logseq-page-name-chars` — Most characters of a page name the client writes.
- `harness-logseq-pages-directory` — Directory of a graph's pages, relative to its root.
- `harness-logseq-search-limit` — Blocks a search returns by default.
- `harness-logseq-search-pages` — Most page files one search reads.
